page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, this instance provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of system memory. The physical topology yields a 1:2 ratio of vCPUs to memory, offering exactly 2.0 GB of RAM per dedicated virtual core.

Network infrastructure on the instance delivers a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps, supporting significant data throughput across distributed cloud topologies. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external cloud storage volumes for all disk persistence and operating system requirements. Additionally, the instance contains zero integrated GPUs and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The 1:2 resource ratio offers an efficient hardware profile for compute-dense scenarios, ensuring infrastructure resources are not wasted on unneeded memory capacity. Because persistent storage and accelerators are absent, workloads must be structured to accommodate network-attached storage latency. The ecs.c9a.16xlarge instance is suitable for CPU-heavy applications, multi-threaded code compilation, distributed continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, and large-scale web servers.
